prompts.title: Recent form — wins, draws, losses
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical frame on GoatLab charcoal #101412. Editorial variant (priority, opens the scene): kinetic typography only. The Spanish headline 'FORMA RECIENTE' locks in from the left in warm white #edf0e6 condensed uppercase with tight tracking; below it the Spanish words 'VICTORIAS', 'EMPATES' and 'DERROTAS' stamp down one after another on a rhythmic two-beat cadence, each landing with a short lime #c5ed74 underline that pulses once and settles. Secondary team chips read 'Como 1907' in lime and 'Manchester United FC' in slate #8ca6bf, sliding in from opposite edges with a single hard shadow each. No axes, no counts, no sample claims in this variant — rhythm and hierarchy carry the meaning. One focal point sits in the upper two thirds under a soft charcoal vignette; the lower quarter stays clear for permanent yellow subtitles.

Statistical variant (from roughly 3s): a grouped count-bar chart. Three categories on the horizontal axis, labelled in Spanish — 'Victorias', 'Empates', 'Derrotas' — each with paired bars, Como 1907 in lime #c5ed74 and Manchester United FC in slate #8ca6bf, separated by a thin warm-white gap. Shared zero baseline, one common count scale in units of 'partidos' printed once at the axis foot, faint single-unit gridlines in warm white. Values resolve from the catalog: {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} against {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Directly beneath the plot a small-caps line reads 'muestra' with {{home.n}} partidos for Como and {{away.n}} partidos for Manchester United, followed by the source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Unequal samples are flagged with outlined capsules around each sample figure — the scale is never renormalised.

Temporal stages on a 9 second cut: 0–3s editorial typography, 3–5s bars rise from the baseline with staggered easing (victorias first, then empates, then derrotas), 5–7s hold while the tallest pair is emphasised with a lime halo and the rest dim to slate, 7–9s the plot lifts and fades. Camera: slow vertical drift upward during the editorial block, then a gentle push-in on the paired bars, never breaking the single focal point. Transition into the chart is a hard lime wipe travelling bottom to top; transition out is a warm-white luminance fade. Exit leaves only charcoal and the subtitle band clean.

prompts.title: Goals for and against — paired bars
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical, GoatLab charcoal #101412 ground. Editorial variant (priority, first beat): an illustrative football pitch drawn in thin warm white #edf0e6 lines, top-down but tilted slightly toward the viewer, occupying the upper two thirds. The two Spanish team names appear as reveal typography — 'Como 1907' in lime #c5ed74 entering from the left touchline, 'Manchester United FC' in slate #8ca6bf entering from the right — while a single abstract lime ball traces a clean, decorative curved path across the pitch markings and settles at the centre spot. The path is purely illustrative: no scoreline, no invented match event, no shot on a real goal. A soft charcoal vignette keeps one focal point; the lower quarter remains empty for permanent yellow subtitles.

Statistical variant: paired bars in a two-by-two arrangement. Two groups sit side by side — Como 1907 on the left, Manchester United FC on the right — each group holding two bars: 'Goles a favor' in lime #c5ed74 and 'Goles recibidos' in slate #8ca6bf. One shared vertical scale in units of 'goles', single zero baseline, faint gridlines in warm white, numeric labels printed above each bar tip in warm white tabular figures. Values resolve from the catalog: {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}} for Como, {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}} for Manchester United. A small-caps annotation under the plot carries the word sample with 'muestra: últimos partidos registrados' and the source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro', keeping provider attribution attached to the data.

Temporal stages across roughly 10 seconds: 0–3s pitch illustration and team reveals, 3–4.5s the pitch desaturates and slides behind as the chart plane arrives, 4.5–7s bars grow upward group by group, 7–9s hold with the attacking bar of each pairing briefly lifted in luminance while the defensive bar steps back, 9–10s exit. Camera: gentle push-in during the ball path, then a flat locked frontal view for the chart so the shared scale stays legible. Emphasis is achieved through luminance and a soft lime glow, never by rescaling. Transition in is a vertical lime wipe; transition out is a slate-to-charcoal dissolve. Educational note on screen in Spanish: 'No es un pronóstico' near the axis foot.

A short narrative emphasis beat lifts the lime name slightly brighter while the slate name recedes, then the emphasis reverses — the tension is visual and rhythmic only, with no counts, no axes and no invented match events. One focal point in the upper two thirds; the lower quarter stays clear for permanent yellow subtitles.

Statistical variant: a compact paired comparison of the two result columns that drive the tension — 'Victorias' and 'Empates' in Spanish — as grouped count bars on a single shared zero baseline, one common scale in units of 'partidos', faint warm-white gridlines, numeric labels printed at bar tips in tabular figures. Como 1907 in lime #c5ed74, Manchester United FC in slate #8ca6bf, thin warm-white gap between paired bars. Values resolve from the catalog: {{home.wins}} and {{home.draws}} against {{away.wins}} and {{away.draws}}. Under the plot a small-caps line prints 'muestra' with {{home.n}} partidos for Como and {{away.n}} partidos for Manchester United, and the source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Only published catalog figures are shown: no model estimate, no forecast and no implied prediction is drawn from this recent sample.

Temporal stages on roughly 9 seconds: 0–3.5s team reveals with divider snap, 3.5–4.5s the divider drops to become the baseline, 4.5–7s grouped bars grow with staggered easing, 7–8.5s hold as the contrast between the two victorias bars is emphasised with a lime halo and the remainder dims, 8.5–9s exit. Camera: locked frontal for the reveal, then a very slow push-in on the emphasised pair; no parallax that would distort the scale.
